requirements.quote:
If the server supplies an empty Certificate message, the client MUST
abort the handshake with a "decode_error" alert.
requirements.condition: a client receives an empty server Certificate message
requirements.why_checkable: An empty server certificate_list can be injected and the client alert observed.

requirements.quote:
If the client does not send any certificates (i.e., it sends an empty
Certificate message), the server MAY at its discretion either
continue the handshake without client authentication or abort the
handshake with a "certificate_required" alert.
requirements.condition: the server receives an empty client Certificate message
requirements.required_behavior: either continue while treating the client as unauthenticated or abort the handshake
requirements.error_behavior: if aborting for the empty client Certificate, send certificate_required
requirements.why_checkable: An empty client certificate_list exposes both explicitly permitted server branches.

requirements.quote:
Also, if some aspect
of the certificate chain was unacceptable (e.g., it was not signed by
a known, trusted CA), the server MAY at its discretion either
continue the handshake (considering the client unauthenticated) or
abort the handshake.
requirements.condition: some aspect of the client's certificate chain is unacceptable
requirements.required_behavior: either continue while treating the client as unauthenticated or abort the handshake
requirements.forbidden_behavior: treat the client as authenticated by the unacceptable chain
requirements.error_behavior: if not continuing unauthenticated, abort the handshake
requirements.why_checkable: A chain failing trust validation can test authentication state and termination behavior.

requirements.quote:
Any endpoint receiving any certificate which it would need to
validate using any signature algorithm using an MD5 hash MUST abort
the handshake with a "bad_certificate" alert.
requirements.condition: an endpoint would need to validate a received certificate using an MD5-based signature algorithm
requirements.forbidden_behavior: validate or accept the certificate chain
requirements.why_checkable: A non-anchor MD5-signed certificate can exercise the mandatory alert branch.

requirements.quote:
SHA-1 is deprecated,
and it is RECOMMENDED that any endpoint receiving any certificate
which it would need to validate using any signature algorithm using a
SHA-1 hash abort the handshake with a "bad_certificate" alert.
requirements.condition: an endpoint would need to validate a received certificate using a SHA-1-based signature algorithm
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept the SHA-1-validated chain without a reason to depart from the recommendation
requirements.why_checkable: A non-anchor SHA-1-signed certificate can exercise the recommended alert branch.
